benchmark_gaps: No performance benchmarks comparing boustrophedon vs spiral vs wavefront vs RRT on identical field shapes and obstacle configurations
No path quality metrics beyond total_distance — missing smoothness, curvature, energy consumption, turn count, headland turn efficiency
No comparison against optimal or near-optimal solutions (e.g., TSP-based pass ordering, convex decomposition lower bound)
No scalability tests: large fields (1000x1000+), many obstacles (100+), fine swath widths, high-resolution grids
No real-world field shape test cases (L-shaped, concave, multi-polygon fields with holes, circular fields)
No timing benchmarks for planning algorithms (planning latency vs field size, vs obstacle count)
No coverage accuracy measurement (actual area covered vs claimed coverage_ratio) — current ratio uses bounding-box approximation
No comparison of grid resolution impact on A*/wavefront path quality and planning time
No benchmark of RRT convergence rate vs step_size, goal_bias, and obstacle density
No Dubins path quality comparison against Reeds-Shepp or other curvature-constrained planners
bottlenecks: Boustrophedon uses bounding box, not actual field boundary — over-covers convex hull area for non-rectangular fields, wasting time/energy/fuel
Coverage ratio calculation is simplified: uses bounding-box area instead of actual polygon area (shoelace formula), giving inaccurate coverage estimates
ObstacleField.avoid_path returns 4 corner points of a square around the obstacle without checking if the path actually intersects the obstacle or computing tangent-based avoidance
Spiral coverage filters out obstacle points but does not reroute — creates discontinuous paths with gaps in coverage
Boustrophedon planner has no obstacle avoidance at all — passes through obstacles
Wavefront DFS path generation creates snake-like paths with excessive backtracking, not efficient coverage
No path smoothing or post-processing (e.g., Bezier curves, shortcutting, Dubins smoothing) — paths are jagged polylines
A* is grid-only with no continuous-space planning — quantization error on coarse grids
No dynamic replanning capability — cannot handle obstacles discovered mid-execution
No multi-robot coordination or task allocation — single-vehicle only
Spiral coverage does not handle non-circular fields — max_radius approximation loses corners
No support for non-holonomic vehicle constraints in coverage planning (Dubins paths exist but are not integrated into coverage planner)
RRT is implemented but RRT* (optimal variant) is missing — paths are not asymptotically optimal
No integration between Dubins path planner and coverage planner — headland turns are not curvature-constrained
ObstacleField only supports circular obstacles — no polygon, line-segment, or compound obstacle support
No segment-obstacle collision detection in ObstacleField — only point-in-obstacle checks
Safety buffer in avoid_path is hardcoded to 1.0 meter — not configurable per operation or vehicle
No geofence or no-fly zone support for regulatory compliance
No terrain/elevation consideration — all planning is 2D
No wind/weather integration for drone-specific planning constraints
missing_algorithms: D* Lite — incremental replanning for unknown or changing environments (discovered obstacles, dynamic replanning)
PRM (Probabilistic Roadmap) — multi-query planning for repeated navigation in the same field
Voronoi-based coverage — maximizes clearance from obstacles, useful for safety-critical operations
Multi-robot coverage — task allocation, region decomposition, and coordination for fleets
Convex decomposition — decompose non-convex fields into convex sub-regions for efficient boustrophedon
STC (Spanning Tree Coverage) — grid-based complete coverage via spanning tree decomposition
Boustrophedon cellular decomposition — partition field into obstacle-free cells, cover each optimally
RRT* — asymptotically optimal variant of RRT for higher-quality paths
Reeds-Shepp paths — extends Dubins to allow backward motion, shorter paths for vehicles that can reverse
TSP-based pass ordering — optimize the order of coverage passes to minimize transit distance
Genetic algorithm / simulated annealing — meta-optimization of coverage paths for complex fields
Morse-based coverage — topological approach using critical points for guaranteed complete coverage
Dijkstra's algorithm — baseline shortest-path for comparison and distance field computation
Zigzag/diagonal coverage pattern — reduce total path length for certain field geometries
Adaptive swath width — variable-rate application support based on soil/pest maps
Headland turn optimization — loop, skip, U-turn, fish-tail patterns with configurable turning radius
Path smoothing / shortcutting — post-process jagged paths into smooth, executable trajectories
Geofencing / no-fly zone support — polygon exclusion zones with automatic path clipping
3D terrain following — constant AGL altitude maintenance over varying terrain
Energy/battery constraint modeling — range-aware planning with recharge stop insertion
Path execution monitoring — deviation detection and recovery behaviors
GPS waypoint export — GPX, GeoJSON, KML formats for drone flight controllers
